speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual combination of symptoms; to narrow this down, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or speaking as well?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; the fluctuating weakness and specific trigger for diplopia are key. Does your condition typically worsen during the day and improve after sleep, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count with Electrolytes and Creatine Kinase. Please also report if you experience any fatigue that worsens significantly after prolonged exercise or specific activities.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain and Cervical Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count with Electrolytes and Creatine Kinase: Not available in current data set. MRI Brain and Cervical Spine: Not available in current data set. Fatigue Assessment: Patient reports weakness worsening after activity that improves with rest, consistent with fluctuating muscle strength; no specific new fatigue reported beyond baseline symptom description.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness that worsens with exertion, diplopia triggered by looking up or down, and lack of sensory deficits is classic for this condition. Given your urgency, these findings are sufficient for a clinical diagnosis, though you will still need an acetylcholine receptor antibody test and potentially a Tensilon test for confirmation.
